source_text: Neque enim in iure cuiusquam est definita suscipere, et quae consequuntur excludere. Qui ergo dicit propter hoc parvulos ad ius diaboli pertinere, quoniam de sexus commixtione generantur; sine dubio ipsam commixtionem, in qua naturae opus est, cum naturae ipsius institutione condemnat.
pass_a_gloss: For it is not in anyone's right to take up defined things and exclude those which follow. He therefore who says that little ones belong to the devil's right on account of this, because they are generated from the mingling of sex; without doubt condemns the mingling itself, in which there is a work of nature, with the institution of nature itself.

lemmas.lexica: LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS parvulus; Blaise infants as Julian's test case
LS opus; Blaise God's works vs devil's

pass_b_english: No one has the right to accept definitions and exclude their consequences. Therefore anyone who says infants belong to the devil’s jurisdiction because they are generated from sexual union undoubtedly condemns that union, in which nature acts, together with nature’s own institution.

choices.why: Julian defends marital union (commixtio) as God's work, not the devil's property.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
